findings.claim: Frontmatter-todo usage is adopted but the status vocabulary has drifted well beyond the ADR-117 schema. ADR-117 §6 specifies todo status as 'pending | completed' only, but live plans use at least: pending, completed, done, dropped, in_progress, plus plan-level statuses strategic-brief, opener, current. The machine-readable intent survives (tooling can still parse it), but the value space is no longer the closed set the ADR defined, which weakens any tooling that branches on status.
findings.quote: status: pending | completed

findings.claim: The drift is predominantly BEHAVIOURAL, not a defect in ADR-117/PDR-018. The exact same lifecycle rules produce clean lanes in product-delivery collections (semantic-search, sdk-and-mcp, security, discovery, connecting-oak-resources all near-zero unindexed) and broken lanes in the self-improvement collections that churn fastest. The discipline is sound; the high-velocity practice lanes are simply not running the archive/index maintenance the ADR requires. The one genuinely STRUCTURAL gap: the lifecycle taxonomy has no sanctioned home for per-session 'opener' artefacts, so they leak into current/ by default.
findings.quote: Archive completed plans promptly after mining outcomes into permanent documentation.

metaFindings.recommendation: Treat this as a behavioural-enforcement gap with one small structural fix, not a redesign of ADR-117/PDR-018 (the discipline demonstrably works where lanes are maintained). Concretely: (1) Add a deterministic gate — a CI/lint check that fails when a current/ or active/ plan has zero pending/in_progress todos (archival overdue), when a plan carries a superseded_by/SUPERSEDED marker outside archive/, or when a current/active plan is unreferenced by any README (reachability). Making the invariant a tripwire artefact (per PDR-029 doctrine the ADR already cites) is the only thing that will hold under the practice-lane churn rate. (2) Close the structural gap: either route session-opener artefacts to .agent/prompts/ as ADR-117 §3 already prescribes, or add an explicit opener/ lifecycle slot exempt from the reachability invariant — then migrate the 14 current/ openers out. (3) Run a one-off consolidation sweep on agentic-engineering-enhancements, observability, agent-tooling and sector-engagement/eef: archive the 33 all-done plans, remove the 4 superseded stubs, and index or relocate the 71 unreachable files. (4) Tighten the ADR-117 §6 todo-status enum to the values actually in use (pending/in_progress/completed/dropped) so the machine-readable contract matches reality. Confidence is high on the reachability, archival, opener and stub findings (all enumerated first-hand); medium on the behavioural-vs-structural attribution, which rests on the clean/dirty split across collections.

findings.claim: Frontmatter-todos compliance is inconsistent. ADR-117 §6 requires all executable plans in current/ and active/ to carry a YAML todos block with machine-readable progress. Of the plans surveyed, 33 files in current/ or active/ lack any todos: block entirely. This includes both legitimate non-plan documents (reports, feature-request notes) and plans that should have todos (e.g. category-integration-remediation.md, no-type-widening-enforcement.plan.md, bulk-data-rebaseline-and-infra-impact-investigation.plan.md). findings.claim: agentic-engineering-enhancements/current/ has accumulated 54 files — the largest single executable lane. This is a structural pressure point: the ADR-117 guidance to 'split the collection or archive completed plans' (PDR-018 §Plan placement) is not being triggered at the density level the estate has reached.

The post-pr-87-merge-pipeline-triage.plan.md is an exemplary execution of the discipline: verified facts are separated from assumptions, speculation is quarantined, and the plan defers to a separate CodeQL plan. The eef-d5-execution.plan.md shows detailed todos with per-item `status: completed` inline, which is correct. The observability/current/sentry-preview-validation-and-quality-triage.plan.md shows superseded phases correctly marked `status: completed` with explicit supersession notes. findings.claim: The stale-executable list (63 files) is dominated by agentic-engineering-enhancements (37) and agent-tooling (14) lanes. The drift is behavioural rather than structural: the architecture (ADR-117, PDR-018) correctly names the required behaviour (archive completed plans promptly, move to active/ before execution, maintain the reachability invariant). No evidence was found that the taxonomy itself is wrong or that the templates are missing. The pattern of 'session ends, complete plans linger, stale list grows' is a session-closure discipline gap, not a flaw in the planning skill or document hierarchy.

metaFindings.recommendation:
Three targeted interventions address the drift without redesigning the architecture.

1. Archival sweep (highest leverage): run a dedicated single-session archival pass across all current/ and active/ lanes to move body-COMPLETE plans into archive/completed/ and add their index entries to completed-plans.md. The 12 confirmed COMPLETE-body plans are the minimum; the full staleExecutable list of 63 is the full scope. This is a behavioural gap in session-closure discipline, not a structural failure.

2. Formalise the opener type: add 'session opener' as a first-class document type in ADR-117 §3 (or create a thin ADR amendment), give it a canonical home outside current/ (e.g. .agent/prompts/session-openers/ or a subdirectory of the collection), and add a lifecycle README note that opener files must not be placed in current/. The 8 existing opener files in agentic-engineering-enhancements/current/ should be relocated or archived after the definition is in place.

3. Enforce frontmatter todos as a lint gate: the 33 no-todos files in executable lanes are a signal that the ADR-117 §6 requirement is unverified at artefact creation time. Either add a markdownlint or custom-lint rule that requires a todos: block in files placed under current/ or active/ (with an explicit allowlist for recognised non-plan document types — .report.md, .feature_request.md, -opener.md), or encode the document-type distinction in the file-naming convention so the rule can target only genuine plans. This converts a behavioural expectation into a structural gate.

metaFindings.headline: The practice estate is genuinely over-weighted at ~41% of live+future plans, but the headline number understates the real problem: both practice collections are clogged with transient session-handoff and PR-snagging debris that was never archived, and the duplicationCandidates list conflates true redundancy with deliberately-coupled parent/child pairs. Fix the lifecycle hygiene first (archive ~30 transient artefacts), then merge the ~8 genuine duplicates; the collection boundaries themselves are sound and should not be redrawn.

findings.claim: The ~38% practice weighting is real (I recomputed 41.1% of non-README live+future plans: aee=87 + agent-tooling=59 = 146 of 355), but the count is inflated by transient artefacts that should not occupy executable lanes at all. Of aee's live+future files, 14 are session 'openers' and disposition/snags stubs; agent-tooling has 8 more. These are handoff debris, not plan estate. Strip them and the practice critical-path plan count drops materially, narrowing the gap with the product path.
findings.quote: status: opener / predecessor_session_napkin_rotation: 1513474e / target_session_shape: five-layer restart pass per PDR-046 + owner direction — this is a session-handoff record sitting in an executable current/ lane, not a plan.

findings.claim: Eleven 'opener' files (status: opener, carrying predecessor-session SHAs) sit in current/ lanes across the two practice collections, and the duplicationCandidates list correctly flags several as overlapping each other (five-layer-restart vs full-napkin-and-comms-graduation; napkin-and-pending-graduations vs full-napkin; collaboration-state-restructure-phase-2 vs collaboration-state-lifecycle-deep-exploration). They overlap because they are successive session openers for the same threads. The cure is not to merge them into one plan — it is to archive all of them, since their sessions have completed.

The observability current/ lane carries six PR-lifecycle/triage artefacts tied to already-merged PRs (pr-93-merge-snagging, pr-93-sonar-quality-gate-resolution with all-completed status entries, pr-87-codeql-alerts, post-pr-87-merge-pipeline-triage, sentry-preview-validation-and-quality-triage, feat-eef-exploration-completion). All six are in the staleExecutable list. The duplicationCandidates correctly notes pr-93-sonar overlaps pr-93-merge-snagging and pr-87-codeql overlaps sentry-preview-triage — but again the cure is archive-on-merge, not merge-the-plans. PR-snagging artefacts are transient by nature and should never persist in a NEXT-up executable lane.

The duplicationCandidates list materially over-reports true redundancy because it conflates deliberately-coupled parent/child and dependency pairs with duplicates. The observability status-page pair is a dependency chain (customer-facing-status-page carries promotion_trigger: statuspage-integration completes — it cannot exist until the other ships); the architecture budget pair is an explicit strategic-parent/executable-child relationship (architectural-budget-system-across-scales is the 'Strategic parent', enforcement-layer the child); the privacy/web-api-gdpr/web-api-security specialist trio is explicitly 'scoped apart; overlap boundaries are well-defined' in the candidates list itself. Merging any of these would destroy intentional structure. Do NOT merge dependency or parent/child pairs.

The two practice collections are WELL-bounded, not over-fragmented. Both READMEs carry an identical, explicit abstraction-level boundary table and the same disambiguation test ('could this plan exist if agent-tools/ did not? If yes it belongs in aee'). aee is practice/governance/doctrine; agent-tooling is the agent-tools/ workspace implementation. Eight files even carry explicit MOVED back-pointers proving the boundary is actively maintained. The over-weighting is a volume problem, not a boundary problem — do not collapse the two collections into one.

A genuinely-redundant cluster worth merging: the agent-tooling collaboration-substrate plans. coordination-watcher-canonicalisation overlaps collaboration-substrate-coordination-rightsizing, and joint-agent-decision-protocol overlaps the same rightsizing m1-inventory. These are same-layer, same-subject plans (the collaboration coordination substrate) rather than parent/child or dependency pairs. This is the one practice cluster where consolidation into a single coordination-substrate plan with phases is warranted.

Genuine same-layer duplicate pairs outside the practice estate that DO warrant merging: architecture quality-gate-hardening vs static-analysis-tool-promotion; architecture doc-architecture-phase-b vs architectural-documentation-excellence-synthesis (candidates note items I3,I6,I7,I8,I9b appear verbatim in both); sdk-and-mcp unified-mcp-server-test-harness vs http-mcp-test-suite-improvements; developer-experience generated-document-pipeline-extraction vs tsdoc-generated-docs-overhaul. These are roughly eight true-duplicate pairs across the whole estate where one is the wider scope and the other a verbatim subset.

The aee collection README is itself a structural smell: it is a 229-line document whose Documents table mixes live plans, completed-archived plans (with strikethrough), eight MOVED back-pointers, and a 30-line linear Read Order chain. A README this dense is no longer a navigable index — it is a second consolidation buffer. This is the volume problem made visible: the collection has accreted faster than it has been curated.

metaFindings.recommendation: Sequence the cleanup in three concrete passes, smallest-risk first. PASS 1 (lifecycle hygiene — biggest win, lowest risk): archive the ~22 transient artefacts that are squatting in executable lanes — the 11 'opener' files and the disposition/snags/ledger stubs in agentic-engineering-enhancements/current, plus the 6 PR-snagging/triage artefacts in observability/current (pr-93*, pr-87-codeql, post-pr-87-triage, sentry-preview-validation, feat-eef-exploration-completion), plus the ws0-disposition and flaky-tests stubs in agent-tooling. Move each to its collection's archive/completed/ after extracting any durable insight per the consolidate-docs workflow. This alone removes ~22 'plans', drops the practice share below the headline figure, and clears the bulk of the duplicationCandidates noise (which is mostly successive openers and PR-snagging pairs, not real plan duplication). Add a repo-validator rule that openers and pr-*/snagging artefacts cannot live in current/ once their session or PR closes. PASS 2 (merge the ~8 genuine same-layer duplicates): consolidate each verbatim-subset pair into the wider-scoped plan with the narrower as a phase — quality-gate-hardening absorbs static-analysis-tool-promotion; the doc-architecture synthesis parent absorbs phase-b's verbatim items; unified-mcp-server-test-harness absorbs http-mcp-test-suite-improvements; tsdoc-generated-docs-overhaul absorbs generated-document-pipeline-extraction; and inside the practice estate, fold coordination-watcher-canonicalisation and joint-agent-decision-protocol into collaboration-substrate-coordination-rightsizing. PASS 3 (do NOT touch): leave the deliberately-coupled pairs alone — the observability status-page dependency chain, the architecture budget parent/child, and the privacy/web-api-gdpr/web-api-security specialist trio are intentional structure, and the aee-vs-agent-tooling boundary is sound and actively maintained. Separately, slim the aee README from a mixed buffer back to a pure index (drop archived/MOVED rows to a footnote, collapse the 30-line Read Order). Net effect: the practice estate stops LOOKING over-weighted because the debris that inflated it is gone, the real duplication shrinks to a handful of legitimate merges, and no load-bearing structure is disturbed.

metaFindings.recommendation:
Four concrete actions, ordered by return on effort:

1. ARCHIVE STALE OPENERS AND COMPLETED PLANS IN CURRENT/ (highest impact, low risk). Move the 9 session-opener files dated 2026-05-06 to 2026-05-12 from agentic-engineering-enhancements/current/ to archive/ — they are handoff documents, not executable plans, and their presence in current/ inflates stale count by ~40%. Also archive the 4 confirmed-complete plans still sitting in current/ (e.g. consolidate-docs-mode-contract IMPLEMENTED 2026-05-27, governance-concepts-and-agentic-mechanism-integration which has all todos: completed). For agent-tooling/current/, archive primary-agent-tooling-enhancements.plan.md (explicitly SUPERSEDED 2026-05-11 by cost-of-collaboration) and pr-102-snagging once its content is absorbed.

2. MERGE THREE CONFIRMED SUPERSESSION PAIRS (clear wins, each owner-ratified already): (a) Archive fitness-frontmatter-manifest-sweep.plan.md — its README entry already says it is absorbed into fitness-token-measurements-and-frontmatter-mandation. (b) Archive http-mcp-test-suite-improvements.plan.md — unified-mcp-server-test-harness.plan.md explicitly declares it subsumes this plan. (c) Merge observability/future/customer-facing-status-page.plan.md into statuspage-integration.plan.md as a Phase 2 section — the status page plan is gated on statuspage integration completing and is 101 lines; merging removes one navigation indirection while the dependency stays explicit.

3. ESTABLISH A PRACTICE-WORK LIFECYCLE GATE (structural, medium effort). The over-weighting problem is partly a scheduling problem: the agentic/current/ queue has ~33 QUEUED or REFERENCE plans that are practice-internal (learning loops, memory systems, specialist capabilities, corpus discoverability) which are not blocking M2 or M3. These should be moved to future/ unless explicitly promoted to the current work window. The rule should be: plans stay in current/ only when they will execute in the active milestone window. This moves the practice estate's visible size from ~38% of live plans to a more proportionate share without losing any work.

4. DO NOT MERGE THE TWO PRACTICE COLLECTIONS. The agentic-engineering-enhancements / agent-tooling split is a deliberate and well-enforced abstraction-level separation (doctrine vs implementation). The README boundary test ('could this plan exist if agent-tools/ did not?') is crisp and actively used. Merging would collapse a useful navigation and ownership signal. The volume imbalance is explained by (a) the opener artefacts inflating stale count and (b) the practice-internal queue depth, both of which are fixed by actions 1 and 3 above.

metaFindings.headline: The critical path is narrow and well-indexed by curriculum-mcp-path-to-ga/roadmap.md, but the only product work genuinely left for M2 close — the user-search widget UI (WS4) — has not started, and that thin path is buried under a ~4:1 ratio of non-product agentic/tooling sprawl with stale index pointers.
metaFindings.recommendation: Treat the critical path as the ~6 plans the roadmap already names, and protect that index from drift. Concretely: (1) Focus the next product work on the one true M2-close blocker — the WS4 user-search widget UI — since the widget is still brand-banner-only; this is the single thing standing between current state and open public alpha. (2) Re-home the two stale index pointers: update sdk-and-mcp-enhancements/active/mcp-app-extension-migration.plan.md so its WS3 reference points at the archived/completed child (and confirm PR #76 merge state) and update observability/active/sentry-observability-maximisation-mcp.plan.md so it stops citing the now-archived mcp-canonical-deploy-shape doctrine plan as 'current execution authority'. Until those two are fixed, anyone walking the path-to-GA index downward hits archived docs and cannot read true status. (3) Bring fix/align_with_upstream_api_spec (129 commits ahead) onto the roadmap as an explicit M2/M3 line item or merge it — unintegrated upstream-spec drift is product-surface risk that the index currently omits. (4) Quarantine the sprawl: agentic-engineering-enhancements (~90 docs) and agent-tooling (~62 docs) are over a third of the estate and carry 159 of the speculative docs; they are practice infrastructure, not the product path. They do not need pruning, but the path-to-GA roadmap should state plainly that they are off the live-product critical path so future sessions stop conflating practice velocity with product velocity. (5) Leave M4/GA undefined as-is — it is correctly gated on owner direction; do not invent gates. Net verdict: the plan estate DOES make the critical path clear at the index level (the roadmap is genuinely good), but stale leaf pointers plus a 4:1 non-product sprawl ratio mean the clarity does not survive one level of navigation, and the single real obstruction (WS4 widget UI) is not being actively worked.

metaFindings.recommendation:
Three concrete actions unblock the path to a live, growing product.

First, for M2 close: the feat/full-sentry-otel-support branch (last commit 2026-03-31, 1,447 commits behind main) must be either merged or explicitly resolved. The branch carries all M2 observability evidence. Given the divergence depth, the choice between rebasing, cherry-picking the material code commits, or treating the evidence as valid for the already-deployed state needs an owner decision now, not when M3 planning begins. Concurrently, WS3 Phase 5 (interactive user-search UI) needs a dedicated session — all its todos are status:pending and it is a named M2 exit gate.

Second, for M3: promote cloudflare-mcp-public-beta-security-gate.plan.md from future/ to current/ immediately, even if Cloudflare account access is still being established. The promotion trigger condition ('when M3 planning begins') is already satisfied. An unexecuted future/ brief cannot gate a milestone. Pair this with opening the A2 privacy/DPIA plan and the A5 Clerk identity ruling — both require Owner+DPO/legal and both block production Clerk launch; deferring them until M2 exits means they will be on the M3 critical path with no runway.

Third, for plan-estate clarity: the roadmap at curriculum-mcp-path-to-ga/roadmap.md is well-structured but its §5 sub-plan inventory needs a 'blocked / stale' column or explicit status markers so a reader can distinguish the four genuinely-active critical-path plans from the 57 stale-executable plans and 112 speculative plans. The current presentation implies a flat, all-in-progress estate that obscures the actual bottleneck. The sentry-preview-validation-and-quality-triage.plan.md in current/ is an example of a stale plan that should move to archive once the branch question is resolved.

metaFindings.recommendation: Do NOT invent new preservation machinery — the repo already has the right instruments (lifecycle taxonomy, reachability invariant, icebox promotion-trigger convention, the semantic-search/future boundary+manifest model). The job is enforcement and generalisation, with zero deletion. Concrete sequence: (1) RE-HOME, don't drop: move the 8 dated `status: opener` files out of agentic-engineering-enhancements/current/ and agent-tooling/current/ into .agent/prompts/ (their declared home), preserving the substance-state map and metacognition pointers each carries. (2) RESTORE REACHABILITY (cheapest, highest leverage): add the missing index files — icebox/README.md (indexing all 13 ideas with their reactivation triggers), observability/future/README.md, security-and-privacy/future/README.md — and reconcile agentic-engineering-enhancements/current/README.md to index all 24 currently-unindexed real plans. This alone un-obscures the speculative inventory without moving a byte of insight. (3) ARCHIVE COMPLETED WORK: extract durable lessons from the merged-PR snagging files (pr-87, pr-93, post-pr-87) into the observability collection README or an ADR, then move them to archive/completed/ — this clears the critical-path lane. (4) CONSOLIDATE ONLY TRUE OVERLAP: for verbatim-superseded pairs (fitness-frontmatter-manifest-sweep -> fitness-token-measurements-and-frontmatter-mandation; primary-agent-tooling -> cost-of-collaboration), keep the superseded file as a back-pointer with insight extracted; do NOT merge deliberately-split complements (statuspage backend/UX, architectural-budget parent/child, privacy/gdpr/security specialists) — give them a disambiguating README instead. (5) GENERALISE THE MODEL: when re-homing speculative future inventory, adopt the semantic-search/future shape (themed _boundary.md folders + adjacent *.research.md companions + a retention-check at any migration) as the standing convention for every collection's future/ lane. Across all five steps the knowledge-preservation principle holds absolutely: every move either keeps the file, adds an index to it, or archives it with its insight extracted first — nothing is deleted.

metaFindings.recommendation:
Four concrete actions, ordered by urgency:

1. URGENT — Triage the 62 stale-executable current/ plans. These are the real critical-path hazard. Each opener file (2026-05-06-*.md) should be checked: if the session they opened has closed, archive the opener to archive/completed/ with a one-line note naming the closing commit. This is a mechanical sweep, not a knowledge-preservation risk — the substance is in the commits the openers reference. Estimate: ~30 of the 62 are openers or have clear superseding plans; archive those first.

2. MEDIUM — Restructure the icebox collection to canonical form (README + lifecycle dirs + promotion triggers), per the already-planned plan-collection-structural-consistency.plan.md Phase 2. Before restructuring: (a) conserve the watcher-liveness-self-heal.md insight by routing it explicitly into comms-watch-liveness-floor.plan.md and claim-liveness-crash-reconciliation-and-session-forensics.plan.md as directed in its own body — its insight is already self-routed; (b) tombstone pair-programming-coach-agent.md pointing to action-time-structural-interrupt-design-space.plan.md and closure-pressure-remediation-design-space.plan.md as the homes that absorbed its insight; (c) tombstone cross-agent-standardisation.md since it self-reports as superseded; (d) keep agent-lifecycle-automation.md and advanced-mcp-server-ideas.md intact — their insight (autonomous commit hygiene, fan-out-fan-in MCP orchestration) is not yet homed elsewhere.

3. HOLD — Do not consolidate the agent-tooling/future/ coordination cluster yet. The collaboration-substrate-coordination-rightsizing M2 ratification is the correct gate — it will produce an owner-vetted supersession list covering liveness-floor, domain-model, watcher-canonicalisation, and adjacent plans. Acting before M2 ratifies the minimal-coordination model would delete load-bearing design inputs before the owner has a chance to weigh them.
